job: Upstreaming a fixed-function transformer-ASIC backend into mainstream serving runtimes so pre-ship customer orders can reach the silicon without a bespoke per-deployment integration
outcome: A merged, documented non-GPU inference backend that lets an existing serving runtime target the transformer ASIC with the model-definition and API surface a GPU already gets
motivation: A billion-dollar pre-ship order book only pays off if real model traffic can reach the fixed-function part through the stacks customers already run

task.who: ASIC vendor software and developer-relations team
task.what: contribute a fixed-function transformer inference backend
task.where: vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM class serving runtimes
task.when: from H2 2026 through H1 2027 ahead of first shipment
task.why: make customer traffic reach the silicon without bespoke integration
task.how: runtime plugin plus proprietary interconnect and shared memory pool

job: Extending a CUDA-centric serving runtime's backend abstraction to accept a non-GPU fixed-function transformer accelerator as a first-class, documented deployment target
outcome: A released serving-runtime version that lists a fixed-function transformer-ASIC backend as a supported target, not a fork, sharing the runtime's model-definition and API surface
motivation: A billion-dollar pre-ship order book is the demand signal that justifies supporting a non-GPU fixed-function target rather than leaving it a fork

task.who: serving-runtime core engineering and maintainer group
task.what: generalize the accelerator backend and scheduler interface
task.where: the runtime's paged-attention and continuous-batching backend layer
task.why: turn backend generality into a feature the serving layer ships
task.how: pluggable backend API decoupling schedulers from a programmable GPU

job: Adding a fixed-function transformer-ASIC option to a managed inference service so tenants can point production traffic at non-GPU silicon through the same deployment path as GPUs
outcome: A managed serving stack that exposes a transformer-ASIC fixed-function inference backend as a documented, first-class deployment path with the existing model and API surface
motivation: Model serving now dominates production spend, so a denser fixed-function serving option is a cost and differentiation lever worth supporting

task.what: onboard a fixed-function transformer backend as a target
task.where: the managed inference control plane and deployment API
task.when: over the runway from H2 2026 to H1 2027
task.why: capture serving spend with denser non-GPU inference silicon
